readings_ruling: AUDIT-1's major finding is resolved. The claim « Prop. 5 is false as printed for r ≤ 0 » is withdrawn everywhere. It has become a question to the author: does « positif » mean > 0 in Déf. 6 and so in Prop. 5? The question carries evidence, and every line of that evidence checks against the transcription. No remaining text asserts the r ≤ 0 falsity as a fact. Each conditional sentence makes the counterexample depend on « positif » including 0. No Lean statement changed. The old and new files elaborate to identical declaration types and definition bodies. The only bold label mark is Déf. 6's. Build, sorry count, axioms and scope are clean. Two leftover wordings are minor (finding 1): the identifier OuvertPleinPrinted and the bold headline of ouvert_plein_counterexample's docstring. Both carry the withdrawn reading when read on their own, but each sits beside a qualifying sentence in the same docstring.

round1_points.notes: Module docstring l.23–30: Prop. 5 is « not marked, pending the reading of « positif » (question) ». Under > 0, ouvert_plein is Prop. 5 as printed. « Only if « positif » includes 0 does the case r = 0 fail. » Checklist l.78 (Déf. 6 r) now reads « r > 0 in the paper's usage, r ≥ 0 under Bourbaki's; question », which is AUDIT-1's proposed wording. Checklist l.87 (Prop. 5 r) reads « ✓ carried: 0 < r, r being a Déf. 6 radius and « positif » read > 0 (question); if « positif » includes 0, the case r = 0 fails ». SCOPE l.92–106 is headed « The radius of Prop. 5 (question, not a finding) ». It is fully conditional, and it says that negative radii are outside Déf. 6 under any reading. The docstrings of ouvert_plein (l.500–504), ouvert_plein_counterexample (l.536–539), OuvertPleinPrinted (l.550–553) and ouvertPleinPrinted_iff (l.559–562) are reworded. Each states that the r = 0 failure is a counterexample to the paper only if « positif » includes 0. In the REPORT, labels[1].findings no longer contains the falsity finding; it keeps only the true redundancy-of-« ouvert » observation. labels[1].hypotheses[2], labels[1].questions[0], labels[0].hypotheses[1] and labels[0].questions[0] are conditional, and notes records the withdrawal. Prop. 5 is still status partial, marked false. A regex sweep of the file and the REPORT for false / as printed / r ≤ 0 / counterexample / refut / fails turns up no unconditional assertion of the falsity. The two leftover wordings are finding 1.
Checklist l.84 now cites « (baseVoisinagesPrinted_iff; OQ-45) ». OQ-56 occurs nowhere in the file. REPORT labels[0].findings[2] still says, correctly, « OQ-56 does not bear on it ».

REPORT labels[0].questions[0] and checklist l.81 now say the following. Under the non-empty reading, the sentence holds for every Déf. 6 radius r > 0 when n ≥ 1 (isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff). It fails only at n = 0 (OQ-45), and at r = 0 if « positif » includes 0. Under Bourbaki's reading it holds in every dimension, both forms are proved, and the Lean is at least the paper. This is AUDIT-1's proposed fix. SCOPE l.115–116 agrees.

This finding was addressed to the master at curation time, not to the closer. REPORT notes record it: OQ-45's text could name Déf. 6 beside Déf. 2–4, together with the basis sentence that fails at n = 0. It is still open for the master.

evidence_check: Every line cited for « positif » = > 0 was checked against papers/benzecri/legacy/labeled/. ch1 l.168–169: « Le groupe multiplicatif $\R^+$ (resp. … » / « … comme groupe des homothéties positives ». ch1 l.205: « \[ F(H)=l^{-1}(\R^+). \] » in Déf. 5, of an open hemisphere. ch1 l.527: « Le groupe $\R^+$ des réels positifs opère sur un cône affin $V$ ». ch2 l.82: « invariant projectif, positif ou nul, appelé pseudo-longueur ». ch2 l.669: « Soit $k$ un nombre réel positif. » Then l.672–675 says that (A, B) ⊂ (M, B) implies ma/ab < k. M = A is allowed and gives 0 < k, so the claim that this forces k > 0 is right. « strictement positif » occurs at ch2 l.366 (Prop. 3), l.382–383 (Déf. 5, the line break falls after « réel ») and l.470 (« un nombre strictement positif »), all correct. Sphere.openHemisphere is defined at Benzecri/Projective/Subvariety.lean:218 as ofCone {v | 0 < l v}, in Benzecri.Sphere. The docstring's attribution « Sphere.openHemisphere, Benzecri.Projective.Subvariety » is therefore correct. The claim « no occurrence of « positif » includes 0 » was checked by listing every positi* occurrence that is not « proposition ». ch1: l.169, 206, 294, 299, 527, 537, 543, 751. ch2: l.82, 343, 366, 383, 412, 470, 669, 689, 758. None reads as ≥ 0. ch2 l.343 is the z coordinate in the open hemisphere, l.751 is reals whose product is 1, and l.412 is Déf. 6 itself. The claim holds. Two further lines would strengthen the question, optionally. ch1 l.534 says « $\R^+$ est homéomorphe au segment ouvert », which is explicit that ℝ⁺ = ]0, ∞[. ch2 l.758 says « Il existe un nombre $r$ positif, tel que tout point $M$ de $V$ possède un voisinage $O_M$ pseudo-boule de centre $M$ et de rayon $r$ ». There a pseudo-ball radius called « positif » must be > 0, since a radius-0 ball is ∅ and is no neighbourhood. Prop. 4 (l.387–391) uses Déf. 5's n(E, k), and Déf. 5 takes k « strictement positif ». So the SCOPE line « its printed broken-line proof (Prop. 4, k > 0) agrees » is correct.

A textual diff against the current file gives 11 hunks, all inside the module docstring (l.24–30, 78, 81, 84, 87, 92–105, 116) or a declaration docstring (l.500–501, 536–539, 550–553, 559–562). The two edit scripts of the fix round (01:02:01Z and 01:02:18Z) replace docstring text only. Both versions were then elaborated in /tmp, each with an appended meta probe. For every non-internal constant of the file, the probe dumps the pretty-printed type, the Expr hash of the type, and the hash of the definition value (pseudoBoule, BaseVoisinagesPrinted, OuvertPleinPrinted). It also runs #print axioms on the 34 REPORT names. The two outputs are byte-identical. The file's 34 declarations are exactly REPORT decls ∪ extra_decls, with nothing missing and nothing extra. All 34 depend on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The /tmp probe directory was deleted afterwards.

findings.what: Two leftover wordings still carry the withdrawn reading when read on their own. (a) The bold headline « **The case `r = 0` of Prop. 5 fails** » presents r = 0 as a case of Prop. 5. The next sentence says that this is a counterexample to the paper only if « positif » includes 0, so the docstring as a whole is accurate, but a hover or a headline excerpt is not. (b) The identifier OuvertPleinPrinted, and the theorem name ouvertPleinPrinted_iff : OuvertPleinPrinted n ↔ n = 0, both say « Printed ». The docstring now defines the predicate as Prop. 5 with pseudoBoule extended to every real radius, which is the printed Prop. 5 only under ≥ 0 and only through r = 0. A reader of the ledger's decl list for the Prop. 5 row sees « ouvertPleinPrinted_iff ↔ n = 0 » and may read the withdrawn claim into it. Nothing asserts the falsity as a fact, and no statement is wrong.
findings.fix: Text only for (a): change the headline to, for instance, « **If radius 0 were a Déf. 6 radius, Prop. 5 would fail** (n ≥ 1) ». For (b), at graduation or at the author's ruling, either rename the predicate (e.g. OuvertPleinAllRadii / ouvertPleinAllRadii_iff; a name change, not a type change), or keep the names and let the docstrings carry the qualification. If the ruling is > 0, both declarations can also move from the Prop. 5 row's decls to extra_decls.
